name: Drinking water; with chlorine disinfection, no adsorption; at consumer
description:
This process reflects treated drinking water at the consumer. Chlorination is the utilized disinfection process. No granular activated carbon adsorption process is included in the treatment system.

This process reflects the full scope of impacts associated with drinking water treatment including acquisition, treatment, distribution and associated infrastructure. 

Inventory data was collected from the Greater Cincinnati Water Works (GCWW) Richard Miller Treatment Plant, which serves a population of 241,000 customers and treats approximately 106 million gallons per day.
category: 22: Utilities/2213: Water, Sewage and Other Systems

processDocumentation.timeDescription: Data collected 2011. Drinking water treatment standards will change over time and with geography. Updating background electricity and input data should maintain process relevance so long as the target treatment system matches the defined system.
processDocumentation.geographyDescription: The case-study facility is located in Cincinnati Ohio and this process reflects the topography and scale of that facility. Background datasets have been selected to represent U.S. average conditions.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: Acquisition, treatment processes: sedimentation, sand filtration, chemical conditioning, primary disinfection - gaseous chlorine, secondary disinfection - sodium hypochlorite, and distribution.
processDocumentation.modelingConstantsDescription: Inventory exchange values were sourced directly from the cited EPA report on disinfection options in municipal drinking water treatment. Background data sources have, in some cases, been updated to reflect newer and/or public data sources. Elementary flows were mapped to the federal elementary flow list.
processDocumentation.completenessDescription: This process aggregates operational impacts. Infrastructure is included via upstream processes. No significant missing flows are known. The mass balance for this process was not calculated.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: Primary data was provided by representatives of the Greater Cincinnati Water Works Richard Miller Treatment Plant.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: Operational inventory values were provided by the case-study facility, in Cincinnati Ohio, per 1000 cubic feet of water treated. The consumption inventory was developed per 1000 cubic feet of water delivered to the consumer assuming that 18.7% of treated water is lost during distribution.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription: This drinking water unit process reflects full scope of flows necessary to estimate environmental impacts of drinking water delivered to the consumer. The scope of the model includes water acquisition, treatment, distribution and infrastructure processes. End-of-life disposal of infrastructure materials is excluded from the model scope. Primary data was provided by representatives of the Greater Cincinnati Water Works Richard Miller Treatment Plant. Uncertainty ranges are not available for this data.
processDocumentation.useAdvice:
This drinking water unit process reflects the full scope of impacts associated with drinking water treatment - which includes acquisition, treatment, distribution and infrastructure. 

This process reflects the context of the case study community. Consider adapting background processes to your context if water treatment is a signficant source of impact within the scope of your assessment. Such adaptations could include substituting in an appropriate regional electricity grid or modifying the included treatment processes.

sources.name: Xue et al (2019) LCA of Urban Water Systems

reviews.details:
Proof reading details: Passed
Other details: none

processDocumentation.intendedApplication:
This drinking water unit process is intended for use as background data by LCA practitioners, industry and the general public. 

Data is sufficient to produce accurate LCIA results for all TRACI impact categories, energy demand, fossil depletion, and water use. 

Situation C2 - Accounting, without system-external interatctions. The intended application is a purely descriptive accounting / documentation of the analysed system excluding existing interactions with other systems in the LCI model.
